{"summary":"I found no BLOCKER in the supplied source. The code logic holds up, but deployment compatibility is not yet proven, and that is where the gaps are.

**What holds up**
- **Voucher redemption:** GET only reads through `previewAutomationVoucher` and never writes. POST checks the origin, then the HttpOnly cookie challenge (HMAC-bound to nonce, issued time, capability and action URL), and only then calls `exchangeAutomationVoucher`.
- **Voucher concurrency:** that function swaps `claimTokenHash` with a conditional `updateMany`. Two different challenges for the same link produce exactly one winner; the loser gets 410. A replay of the same challenge rebuilds the same bearer through `retry()`.
- **Magic link:** GET runs only `eligible()` (verify plus a tenant lookup). POST checks the tenant before calling `consumeStudentPortalAccessToken`.
- **Body safety:** the limiter adapter copies only the URL, method and headers, so it never reads or splits the request body.
- **Native preview mode:** it re-reads the environment at call time, so a caller-supplied config cannot enable it. It requires Upstash and fails closed with 503.

**Remaining gaps (all deployment and integration)**
1. **Missing or wrong setting causes an outage.** If `ENTRY_CLIENT_IP_TRUST_MODE` is unset or wrong, every entry family returns 503 and nothing checks this before deployment. The referral route hides the failure: it still redirects to the plans page but silently drops attribution.
2. **No proven Production mode.** Native mode is Preview-only. Trusted-proxy mode needs an injected proof header plus an `x-real-ip` that is really the client's address. That combination is contradictory on direct Vercel and keys on the fronting proxy's addresses when another proxy sits in front.
3. **Live chat breaks in a full native-preview deployment.** Live chat still picks its trust mode from `RATE_LIMIT_PROVIDER`. With Upstash it requires the proof header, so chat writes would return 403. Chat reads and purchase broadcasts would share one global "unknown" bucket.
4. **One proof header, two secrets.** Entry and live chat check the same header against two separate environment secrets.
5. **Effective limits depend on the provider.** With `cloudflare_waf` the app enforces nothing, so the new paths depend on WAF rules for which there is no evidence. With `memory`, limits are per instance.
6. **Magic-link double submit.** Unlike the voucher flow, a double-submit on the magic-link confirmation shows an "invalid or expired" error after the first request has already used the link.
7. **Shared-IP admission limit (low confidence).** Live admission keeps a per-IP limit of 120/min. Viewers behind one shared address, or one IPv6 /64 in native mode, could hit it.

The test and browser receipts you supplied show none of the following: the native-preview full deployment, a staging environment matrix, WAF rule coverage, or live chat under the new modes.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","file":"src/lib/trusted-entry-rate-limit.ts","area":"entryIpTrustConfig() fallback `return { trustMode: "none", deploymentSource: "none" }` and checkRateLimit `if (!ip) return 503`; consumers src/app/r/[code]/route.ts limited branch, live-admission, portal access, voucher redeem","issue":"Any environment that has not explicitly set a matching ENTRY_CLIENT_IP_TRUST_MODE/DEPLOYMENT_SOURCE pair (and the ingress secret for cloudflare/trusted-proxy) resolves to `none`. Every opted-in entry route then returns 503. No readiness or boot-time validation is shown. In /r/[code], a 503 'source unavailable' is handled the same as a 429: the user is redirected to /billing/plans with no attribution and no error signal.","evidence":"entryIpTrustConfig ignores RATE_LIMIT_PROVIDER and defaults to `none`. checkRateLimit returns a 503 with Retry-After 30 when ip is null. The referral route converts any non-null `limited` into a plain redirect. The task states that the existing staging was not modified and the full patch was not deployed.","impact":"Deploying this patch to an existing staging or production environment without the new env vars would block magic-link login (GET and POST), voucher redemption, live playback admission and release (live-admission errors also return 503, so they are indistinguishable), and would silently drop all referral attribution.","recommended_fix":"Add a deploy or readiness gate that fails, or a health check that reports, when the resolved entry config is `none` in a deployed environment. Document the required ENTRY_* variables for each environment. In the referral route, separate the 503 source-unavailable case from a 429 by logging or counting it so a misconfiguration is visible.","required_test":"Add a unit test over the env matrix for each declared deployment profile (preview-native, production, staging, local e2e) asserting a non-`none` resolution. Add a referral route test showing that the 503 source-unavailable case is observable (log or metric) and distinct from a 429. Run a staging smoke test of magic-link, voucher, admission and referral with the real env set.","confidence":0.7},{"severity":"MAJOR","file":"src/lib/trusted-entry-rate-limit.ts","area":"entryIpTrustConfig trusted-proxy/cloudflare branches; request-client-ip.ts trusted-proxy branch (x-real-ip + LIVE_CHAT_INGRESS_PROOF_HEADER)","issue":"No ENTRY mode has been shown to work for Production. `vercel-native` is deliberately limited to VERCEL_ENV=preview. `trusted-proxy` requires a secret proof header that direct Vercel ingress cannot inject. If a fronting proxy injects it instead, Vercel's x-real-ip and x-forwarded-for hold that proxy's egress address, so all clients collapse into a few buckets (the shared-IP failure this WP is meant to fix). `cloudflare` mode is valid only for a Cloudflare-fronted topology, and no evidence for that topology was supplied.","evidence":"vercel-native requires `env.VERCEL_ENV === "preview"`. trusted-proxy requires hasValidIngressProof and then uses `x-real-ip` as the client address. Evidence covers only Chromium and Firefox locally plus an earlier proof of the native-preview helper.","impact":"On a Production rollout you would have to choose between a total entry-route outage (see the previous finding) and a misattributed client identity that recreates the shared-IP throttling across all users.","recommended_fix":"Declare the Production topology explicitly and provide a mode that matches it, either native Production with the same server-side metadata checks or a documented fronting proxy that overwrites both the proof header and the client-IP header. Until then, add a release blocker saying Production entry routes are not supported.","required_test":"Run a deployed probe on the target Production-like topology from two different egresses. Assert distinct bucket identities, and assert that a spoofed proof header or spoofed x-real-ip/x-vercel-forwarded-for is rejected or ignored.","confidence":0.55},{"severity":"MAJOR","file":"src/lib/live-chat-request-security.ts","area":"liveChatIpTrustConfig upstash branch; consumers api/live-chat/messages, api/live-chat/private, api/live-purchase-broadcasts","issue":"Live chat still picks its trust mode from RATE_LIMIT_PROVIDER. In the native-preview topology the ENTRY routes require (RATE_LIMIT_PROVIDER=upstash_redis, direct Vercel), live chat resolves to `trusted-proxy`, which needs a LIVE_CHAT_INGRESS_SECRET proof header that direct Vercel never sends. Chat and private-chat writes then return 403. Reads and purchase broadcasts get `clientIp = null`, which rateLimitRequestWithIdentity turns into `cf-connecting-ip: unknown`, so all viewers share one 60/min (chat read) or 120/min (broadcasts) bucket.","evidence":"In securityGate (messages) and security (private), `requireTrustedClientIp` is false for GET. rateLimitRequestWithIdentity sets `clientIp ?? "unknown"`. live-purchase-broadcasts calls checkRateLimit with trustedIp, which may be null. The task notes that the live chat deployment config differs from ENTRY and that the browser suite does not prove the full native-preview deployment.","impact":"In a full native-preview deployment, viewers could be admitted to playback but could not post chat. Chat reads and purchase broadcasts would be throttled globally, and one client could exhaust that shared bucket for everyone. ENTRY fails closed with 503 while chat silently degrades into a shared bucket, which is inconsistent.","recommended_fix":"Have live chat use the same resolved identity as the entry wrapper, or a shared resolver that understands vercel-native. At minimum, return 503 or 403 when the read identity is null instead of using a shared 'unknown' bucket, and state explicitly that live chat is unsupported in vercel-native until migrated.","required_test":"Add an env-matrix unit test: the vercel-native preview env must give live chat a non-null identity, or the routes must fail with an explicit status. Add a route test showing that null-identity GETs never share a global bucket. Run a deployed native-preview check of chat post/read and purchase broadcasts.","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"MINOR","file":"src/lib/request-client-ip.ts","area":"LIVE_CHAT_INGRESS_PROOF_HEADER used by hasValidIngressProof for both ENTRY_CLIENT_IP_INGRESS_SECRET and LIVE_CHAT_INGRESS_SECRET","issue":"The entry and live chat families check the same header (`x-celebratedeal-live-chat-ingress`) against two independently configured secrets. The edge can inject only one value, so the two secrets must always be identical. Nothing enforces or checks that.","evidence":"entryIpTrustConfig passes `env.ENTRY_CLIENT_IP_INGRESS_SECRET`. liveChatIpTrustConfig passes `env.LIVE_CHAT_INGRESS_SECRET`. Both go to hasValidIngressProof, which reads the same header constant.","impact":"Rotating or setting one secret without the other silently breaks one family: entry routes return 503, or chat writes return 403 and reads fall into the shared bucket.","recommended_fix":"Use a single secret variable for both families, or give entry its own header name. Add a startup check that both secrets match while they share a header.","required_test":"Add a unit test where the two secrets differ that expects a readiness failure, or that shows the families no longer share a header.","confidence":0.55},{"severity":"MINOR","file":"src/lib/trusted-entry-rate-limit.ts","area":"checkRateLimit delegation to checkLegacyRateLimit for cloudflare/trusted-proxy modes","issue":"Only vercel-native requires upstash_redis. In cloudflare mode with RATE_LIMIT_PROVIDER=cloudflare_waf, the legacy limiter returns null, so the 30/60/120 per-minute limits on the new keys are not enforced in the app. They depend on WAF rules for /portal/*/access, /api/automation/vouchers/redeem, /r/* and /api/live-admission, and no evidence for those rules was supplied. With provider=memory, the limits are per instance.","evidence":"rate-limit.ts has `if (provider === "cloudflare_waf") return null`. entryIpTrustConfig does not check the provider in the cloudflare or trusted-proxy branches.","impact":"The confirm/redeem/admission throttling promised by the code may not exist in a WAF or serverless-memory deployment.","recommended_fix":"Constrain allowed provider combinations per mode, as native mode already does, or list the required WAF rules for each new route and key as release evidence.","required_test":"Add an env-matrix test that rejects, or at least flags, cloudflare+memory and trusted-proxy+memory. Add release evidence that the WAF rules exist for the new paths and methods.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"MINOR","file":"src/app/portal/[vendorSlug]/access/route.ts","area":"POST: consumeStudentPortalAccessToken → `if (!claim) return failure()`","issue":"The voucher flow explicitly supports resending the same challenge (deterministic bearer plus a retained cookie). The magic-link POST does not. A double-click or a resubmit after a lost response consumes the token on the first request, and the second request redirects to login?error=invalid_or_expired. If the browser cancels the first navigation, the user can end up on the error page and may not be logged in.","evidence":"On consume failure the route calls failure(), which clears the challenge and redirects to the error page. It does not check whether this same challenge already succeeded.","impact":"Users can get a confusing login failure and lose a single-use link, which forces them to request a new email.","recommended_fix":"Treat a repeat of the same verified challenge the way the voucher flow does. For example, record the consumed challenge digest so a repeat redirects to the portal, or redirect to the portal when a valid session for that vendor already exists, before reporting invalid_or_expired.","required_test":"Add a Playwright test that double-submits the confirmation form (and one that replays the same form and cookie after success) and asserts that the user ends up logged into the portal.","confidence":0.4},{"severity":"MINOR","file":"src/app/api/live-admission/route.ts","area":"POST checkRateLimit(request, "live-admission", 120, 60_000)","issue":"Admission is a per-viewer lease renewal (TTL 90s), but the limit is per client identity. In native mode that identity is a whole IPv6 /64 or one IPv4 NAT address. A classroom, office or carrier NAT with more viewers than about 120/min divided by the renewal rate will hit a 429 and lose playback. Unlike live interactions (1,200/min open bucket), this limit was not adjusted for shared IPs.","evidence":"LIVE_VIEWER_SESSION_TTL_MS = 90_000. Native bucket identity collapses IPv6 to a /64. Admission is limited to 120/min per identity.","impact":"Playback could be interrupted for large audiences behind one shared address, which is the scenario this WP targets.","recommended_fix":"Document the client renewal interval and set the admission limit to cover the expected shared-IP audience. Alternatively, key renewals on a valid existing viewer token in addition to the IP.","required_test":"Add a load test or unit test that simulates N viewers behind one identity renewing at the client's real interval and asserts no 429s at the target audience size.","confidence":0.3}]}
